pr_title: deCONZ - Fix service device refresh calling state update
pr_body:
## Description:
Unintentional behavioural change when updating data management in pydeconz. This allows controlling whether or not an update should be ignored.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #30890

comments: I can confirm this behavior. This is not good. Lights turns on or off randomly in my house when I run a device_refresh. It never did this before

@KennethLavrsen could you please specify bridgeid in service parameter and try to call service.
I'm getting error:
```
'00212EFFFF012345'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/websocket_api/commands.py", line 134, in handle_call_service
    connection.context(msg),
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 1226, in async_call
    await asyncio.shield(self._execute_service(handler, service_call))
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 1251, in _execute_service
    await handler.func(service_call)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/deconz/services.py", line 56, in async_call_deconz_service
    await async_refresh_devices_service(hass, service_data)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/deconz/services.py", line 123, in async_refresh_devices_service
    gateway = hass.data[DOMAIN][data[CONF_BRIDGEID]]
KeyError: '00212EFFFF012345'
```

It seems that deconz.device_refresh activates my scripts which toggles light states.
```
Script script.toggle_hue_light already running.
15:52 components/script/__init__.py (WARNING)
Script script.toggle_zigbee_light already running.
15:52 components/script/__init__.py (WARNING)
'00212EFFFF025C47'
15:52 components/deconz/services.py (ERROR) - первое сообщение получено 15:51
```

@bastshoes 
I use the command without any bridgeid. You only need it if you have more deconz instances as I know it. And if you use it you need to use the right one. 00212EFFFF012345 is not the right one. It is the example one. And by the way - from 0.104.x the 4  F's need to be removed so a valid ID now lookslike 00212E012345

This bug is pretty serious

It is not the devices that toggles. It is the sensors are trigger all automations that make everything flicker and toggle

When I came home and tried the deconz.device_refresh the whole house went mad because I use deconz sensors everywhere.

Alarm system can go off. My toilet flushed. My TV and amplifier turned on.

This is a serious bug. We cannot have all sensors triggering just because Home Assistant refreshes devices. It may seem not so important but if the code that discovers devices later gets triggered in other cases then I can risk water flooding and burgler alarms causing havoc when I am not home. I really do not like this

When I run a refresh more than 650 actions are logged from automations being triggered. Including my z-wave sirens being triggered. This is really scary
@KennethLavrsen even with removed F's I'm getting same error.

Hey there @kane610, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`deconz`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L75) for? Thanks!

I tried to investigate more to help debugging.

I started the event viewer to listen to deconz_event.

And what happens is that every deconz sensor and remote in my setup report each ONE event. Most aare x002 event but also x003 events are seen. So Home Assistant is triggered by all these events and that triggers all my automations. So it seems that Home Assistant tells deconz to dump all its devices and this is misinterpreted as events.

So either the deconz integration was changed so it asks for more info from the deconz API than before. Or it parses the returned info in a new way triggering false events.
I think I know why this happens, is it only sensors that are affected and trigger updates?

As far as I can see, yes

It is my remote controls and window sensors. All that trigger events

So the root cause of this is that I've restructured the whole library on how it handles data, so the device refresh service not only reads in new devices but updates states on all known devices as well. Yet again an unintended side effect. I was too effective during Christmas :P

I will try to get a fix together during the weekend for this. It is quite busy so I can't guarantee exactly when its fixed. I have one idea that might be really simple to implement

review_comments: Shouldn't you check here for `ignore_update` too ?
No it is just tracker for battery sensors, by not evaluating ignore_update we increase the chance of creating new battery sensors which would be a good thing :)
This seems kinda weird. Wouldn't it be possible to just not call `async_update_callback` if `ignore_update` is True ?
My thought was to not have that logic in the library, but you think that would be better?
